deep.reconstruction:
WHAT THE PAGE IS. Each block is headed 'p.h', where p is a prime with p ≡ 5 (mod 8) and h is the number of properly primitive classes of positive binary forms (a,b,c) = ax^2+2bxy+cy^2 of determinant b^2-ac = -p. In modern terms h = h(-4p). The primes are 2213, 2141, 2069, 2053, 2029, 1997, 1973, 1949. These are exactly all primes ≡ 5 mod 8 in [1949, 2213], in descending order. The run continues from the previous page (2437…2221) and into the next (1933…1621). Every h is ≡ 2 (mod 4), as it must be: for p ≡ 5 mod 8 the 2-part of the class group is Z/2.

THE COLUMNS. Under each heading Gauss lists the powers f^k, k = 0, 1, …, h/2, of one chosen prime form f = (q, b0, c0). Here q is the smallest suitable odd prime with (-p/q) = 1.
- f = (3,1,(p+1)/3) for 2213, 2141, 2069, 1997, 1949.
- f = (7,1,(p+1)/7) for 2029 and 1973.
- f = (11,2,187) for 2053.
Each entry 'a.b' records the reduced form f^k, with a its first coefficient and b its middle coefficient, normally taken mod a and up to sign. Since f^-k has the same a, only k ≤ h/2 is needed.

THE CYCLICITY TEST. The class f^(h/2) must be the unique non-principal ambiguous class (2,1,(p+1)/2). So every completed column ends in '2'. If f^(h/2) = (2,1,…) and no earlier power is principal, then f has order h and the class group is cyclic, i.e. the determinant is 'regular' in the sense of Disquisitiones Art. 306.

WORKING FROM BOTH ENDS (my inference). Gauss also fills columns from the bottom, using f^(h/2-k) = g·f^(-k) with g = (2,1,(p+1)/2). This gives tails such as 18, 6, 2 (from 2·9, 2·3, 2) or 14, 2 (from 2·7), and the two halves meet in the middle.

SAMPLE STEPS (composition, then reduction), all checked by me:

p = 2141, h = 78:
- (3,1,714)^2 = (9,1,238).
- f^3 = (27,10,83) ~ (27,-10,…), i.e. b ≡ ±10 mod 27, b ∈ {10, 17}.
- f^4: compose to a = 81. b ≡ 17 mod 27 with b^2 ≡ -2141 mod 81 gives (81,17,30) ~ (30,-17,81) ~ (30,13,77). Written '30.17'.
- f^5 = (30,17,81)(3,1,714) with gcd(30,3,18) = 3 gives (10,7,219), written '10.7'.
- f^6 = (30,7,73).
- f^7: a = 90, b = 37, giving (90,37,39) ~ (39,2,55), written '39.2'.

p = 2069, h = 38:
- 27.19: 19^2 + 2069 = 2430 = 27·90.
- 30.11: (81,19,30) ~ (30,11,73).
- Tail: f^17 = 18 → (18,1,115), f^18 = (6,1,345), f^19 = (2,1,1035).

p = 2053, h = 18, f = (11,2,187):
- f^2 = (121,2,17) ~ (17,15,…) [15 ≡ -2].
- f^3 = (26,1,79); 29.8 → (29,8,73); 43.22 → (43,22,59).
- f^6 written '13.64': 64 ≡ -1 mod 13, an unreduced middle coefficient for (13,±1,158).
- f^8 = 22 = 2·11, f^9 = (2,1,1027).

p = 2029, h = 34, f = (7,1,290):
- f^2 = (49,15,46) ~ (46,31,…), written '46.31'.
- The 5-form occurs as f^12. It has order 17, which explains why Gauss did not use the 5-form as generator.
- The column continues at the top of the third column, rows 4–17, ending 14, 2.

p = 1973, h = 42, f = (7,1,282):
- f^2 = (49,43,78) ~ (41,6,49).
- The 3-form is f^15, of order 14. Again this is why 3 was not used.

p = 2213, h = 42:
- a-sequence 1, 3, 9, 27, 37, 39, 13, 39, 22, 43, 46, 23 for k = 0..11. I verified each of these, e.g. f^4 = (81,28,37) ~ (37,9,62); f^9 = (66,25,43) ~ (43,18,59).
- The overwriting at row 9 (ending in 43) fits a corrected sign choice.

p = 1997, h = 42:
- 33.26: (81,55,62) ~ (62,7,33) ~ (33,-7,62), and -7 ≡ 26 mod 33.

p = 1949, h = 70:
- 9.7, 27.7 (b = 7, c = 74); 29.20 from (81,61,29) ~ (29,-20,81).
- The column is complete to f^35 = (2,1,975).

INCOMPLETE COLUMNS. The tables for 2213, 2141 and 1997 are not finished.

THE BOX OF SUMS.
- '5. 78.42.38.34.18 / 210' is the class numbers of 2141, 2213, 2069, 2029, 2053 sorted decreasingly. The sum 78+42+38+34+18 = 210 is correct.
- The previous page has the analogous '10 … 336'. The next page has '15) … 518, 34 8/15'; that list includes 70, 42, 42 for 1949, 1973, 1997.
- '29. 1202 .82' and '1. 18*' look like running totals or a frequency count of class numbers; their exact meaning is not certain.
- Purpose: empirical study of the size and average of h(-4p) for prime determinants, alongside the cyclicity check.
errors: p = 2141, row 3: the entry reads '27.16', but the form (27,b) of determinant -2141 requires b ≡ ±10 mod 27 (b = 10 or 17). 16^2 + 2141 = 2397 is not divisible by 27. The next entry 30.17 follows from b = 17, so this is either a slip of the pen or the digit is really 17.
p = 1997, row 13: the mark read as '1' cannot be f^13, since the principal class cannot recur before k = h = 42. It is probably a stray mark, a different digit, or an unfinished entry.
p = 2053, row 6 '13.64': the middle coefficient is unreduced (64 ≡ -1 mod 13). Not an error, just unreduced notation.
Several columns (2213, 2141, 1997, and the middle of 1973 and 2029) are left incomplete. The cyclicity check is therefore not finished on this page for those p.

results.what: Computation of successive powers of a prime form (composition plus reduction) for determinants -p, p ≡ 5 mod 8, to show it has order h and hence that the class group is cyclic (regular determinant)
results.modern_name: Cyclicity of the class group Cl(-4p); order of a prime ideal class via composition (cf. baby-step/two-ended computation of the class-group structure)

results.what: Using the ambiguous class (2,1,(p+1)/2) as f^(h/2) to fill the table from both ends (f^(h/2-k) = g·f^(-k))
results.modern_name: Exploiting the 2-torsion element of a cyclic group of order h ≡ 2 mod 4; meet-in-the-middle order verification

results.what: Class numbers h(-4p) for all primes p ≡ 5 mod 8 between 1949 and 2213 (42, 78, 38, 18, 34, 42, 42, 70), with grouped sums and averages
results.modern_name: Class number tables and empirical mean of h(-4p)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Nachlass class-number tables, Werke II); averages cf. DA Art. 302

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine computational working for Gauss's known class-number tables and his study of regular (cyclic) determinants and class-number averages. Both are documented in the Disquisitiones and in the Werke II Nachlass. Nothing here is beyond what he is known to have done.

Entries 27.19, 30.11, 18, 6 for p = 2069 are valid forms
